Her sudden removal shifted the competitive landscape, as remaining athletes now hurry to seize valuable podium opportunities in the final heptathlon events.
title: Disqualified over footwear! Iran’s Fatemeh out of heptathlon in dramatic setback

author: DHRUV YADAV
description: The US Air Force is integrating Collaborative Combat Aircraft into its operational framework, enhancing aerial combat capabilities. This move aims to improve situational awareness and reduce risks to manned platforms in contested environments. The two new aircraft, General Atomics' YFQ-42A and Anduril's YFQ-44A, are currently undergoing testing. Manned-Unmanned Teaming is a key feature, allowing pilots to direct unmanned assets in combat.
title: How AI powered autonomous drones are reshaping aerial combat

author: PRIYANKA JAISWAL
title: ‘BrahMos made in UP giving Pakistan sleepless nights’: Amit Shah

author: SHIVANGHI PAYAL
description: India is currently grappling with a host of challenges tied to its international relations, fluctuating energy prices, and evolving AI technology. V Anantha Nageswaran, the Chief Economic Adviser, highlighted the critical need to bolster manufacturing and attract foreign investments. He pointed out the ongoing goods trade deficit, urging for more robust policies to enhance capital inflows.
title: CEA flags 3 'near term' headwinds for Indian economy: What are they

author: AADRITA HALDER
title: ‘Dead mindset cannot see vibrancy’: Amit Shah on Rahul’s ‘dead economy’ remark

author: NITESH DUBEY
description: During the second Test match in Colombo, Yashasvi Jaiswal found himself in a heated exchange with Asitha Fernando after a wicket fell. India’s wicketkeeper-batter, Dhruv Jurel, disclosed that Jaiswal endured ongoing verbal provocations from Fernando post-dismissal. While Jaiswal was open to the competitive banter, he firmly rejected any personal slurs. The altercation intensified, forcing players to step in to separate the two.
title: 'Nonstop abuse': Dhruv Jurel reveals what triggered Jaiswal's clash with Fernando

author: ARYAN SINGH
description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has raised concerns regarding the possibility of US military action against Canada under extreme circumstances. This remark comes amidst escalating trade tensions between the two nations. The stark differences in military budget and resources underline Canada's ongoing commitment to modernizing its defense capabilities and reinforcing its Arctic strategies, while both countries continue to work together under NORAD for North American defense.
title: Canada says it considered risk of US attack: How their militaries compare

author: PRIYA SRIVASTAVA
description: Sidharth Maheshwari's insights shed light on the often misleading nature of CTC figures in the job market. For instance, an attractive salary of ₹85 lakh includes various elements such as fixed pay, bonuses, and variable compensation. However, after mandatory deductions like taxes and other non-cash perks, the actual take-home can drop considerably. Therefore, job seekers must be aware of these salary intricacies to ensure they make financially sound choices.
title: Manager with Rs 85 lakh package reveals how much he actually gets each month

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: Google will launch a prototype satellite named MVP aboard SpaceX's Transporter-18 mission scheduled for October 1. This initiative is part of Project Suncatcher, which explores creating scalable machine learning infrastructure in space. Google CEO Sundar Pichai emphasized the necessity of this research for future computing demands. The project is designed to forecast the processing needs of next-generation AI technologies and aims to establish data centers in space.
title: Google hitches a ride aboard Elon Musk's SpaceX; to send TPUs to space

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
title: Norfolk seal rescued with 4kg debris around neck faces months of rehabilitation

author: TOI REAL ESTATE DESK
description: A Georgia landowner claimed a $23 million charitable tax deduction after donating a 103-acre conservation easement, arguing the property could have been used as an aggregate quarry. The US Tax Court rejected the proposed quarry use, valuing the easement at $480,000. The 11th Circuit upheld the valuation and a 40% gross valuation misstatement penalty.
title: Georgia landowner claimed $23m tax break; court backs $480,000 valuation

author: HIJAM RAJU SINGH
description: Hockey India president Dilip Tirkey has filed a police complaint against several officials for misconduct. The complaint includes allegations of criminal breach of trust and theft of personal belongings. This development follows ongoing disputes between Tirkey and secretary general Bhola Nath Singh over administrative issues. The dispute intensified after a controversial jersey color change allegedly made without Tirkey's approval.
title: HI row escalates: Tirkey files Delhi Police complaint over ‘criminal breach of trust’

author: RAJEEV SINGH
description: Russian governor Yuri Slyusar said around 50 drones were destroyed over the region and the strike forced the refinery to temporarily suspend operations. He said there were no reports of casualties there. In Ulyanovsk, eight people were injured after another drone attack damaged industrial and civilian infrastructure, Governor Alexei Russkikh said. The region is home to a major electronics plant.
title: Ukraine strikes Russian oil refinery, train in overnight drone attacks; 2 killed

author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
description: Antonio Tajani ignited controversy with his remarks on women's attire during a political gathering in Italy, linking skirt length to a woman's dependability and marriage prospects. In defiance, female opposition senators donned miniskirts in the Senate, boldly asserting their personal choice in fashion while disputing societal stereotypes. Following considerable public outcry, Tajani issued an apology, sparking vital dialogues about women's rights and empowerment.
title: Italian women politicians post miniskirt photos after minister’s motherhood remark

author: VIJAYA SRIVASTAVA
description: Across India, demonstrations erupted as citizens rallied for the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. In Assam, Congress leaders confronted police barricades and were detained while protesting, even trying to set fire to an effigy of Kumar in criticism of his oversight of electoral rolls. Security in Delhi was bolstered in expectation of similar unrest, reflecting growing political tensions regarding the commission's recent actions.
title: EC-SIR row: Jantar Mantar entrance barricaded ahead of protests - video

author: SHIVANGHI PAYAL
description: FSSAI has proposed amendments to prohibit the labeling of non-dairy products as "Paneer". This change aims to protect consumers from misleading marketing practices. The proposal affects both packaged goods and food businesses using substitutes. Stakeholders have been invited to provide feedback on these proposed regulations. Increased scrutiny of food safety and labelling practices has prompted this regulatory action to prevent consumer deception.
title: Is your 'paneer' really paneer? What FSSAI's latest proposal could change for you

author: PRACHI KUMAWAT
description: Women wrestlers have challenged the acquittal of former Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh and co-accused Vinod Tomar in the sexual harassment case before the Rouse Avenue court. Special Judge (MP-MLA Cases) Dig Vinay Singh is scheduled to hear the appeal on Saturday.
title: Brij Bhushan sexual harassment case: Women wrestlers challenge acquittal

author: SHIVANGHI PAYAL
description: Nirmala Sitharaman clarified that there will be no Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) charged by the government on UPI transactions. She reassured consumers that for transactions over Rs 2,000, the MDR will be covered by merchants and banks. According to NPCI’s Dilip Asbe, a significant 75 percent of UPI transactions remain unaffected by MDR. Most fees originate from larger businesses that incur higher credit card charges.
title: ‘Not a government issue’: FM Sitharaman explains where UPI MDR charge goes

author: TOI REAL ESTATE DESK
description: In India, homebuyers can seek interest compensation for delays in property possession from developers. Recent judicial decisions confirm that taking possession does not forfeit the right to claim such interest. Notably, the Allahabad High Court supported a homebuyer over a substantial delay in receiving possession. Claims can rely on agreements, payment records, and RERA regulations, emphasizing the importance for buyers to understand their rights amid developer delays.
title: Got keys to your home after years of delay? You may still claim interest for lost time

author: RAJEEV SINGH
description: The planned meeting was announced after the foreign ministers of the three countries met in New York on Thursday. Saudi foreign minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan, Pakistan's deputy prime minister and foreign minister Ishaq Dar, and Turkish foreign minister Hakan Fidan discussed the attacks and possible steps under the agreement.
title: Pumping life into Mecca Pact? Saudi, Turkey, Pak plan meet against Houthis threat

author: AMIT KUMAR
description: After waiting 15 years to wear the India jersey, shot putter Krishna Jaisankar is finally ready for her Asian Games debut in Japan. From injuries and missed opportunities to breaking her own national record with a 17.35m throw, Krishna has learned to never give up. Now, with an 18m target and LA 2028 dream in sight, the 23-year-old says: “All right, it’s showtime.”
title: '15 years ... I waited for long': Krishna Jaisankar set for her India moment at Asiad

author: SAURABH THAKUR
description: A 73-year-old senior citizen faced difficulties due to the absence of a promised Western toilet at Chittorgarh railway station. He initially received a minimal refund and compensation from IRCTC but sought more due to his hardships. The Chandigarh state consumer commission deemed the original compensation insufficient and raised it significantly to Rs 20,000. The commission ordered IRCTC and Indian Railways to refund the original amount with interest.
title: Western toilet promised on IRCTC portal but not provided; commission orders Rs 20k

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
description: A study by Colorado State University reveals that saffron flourishes under semi-shaded solar panels, yielding better results than those without shade. By integrating rooftop farming with renewable energy, urban food production can tackle space constraints. Projections suggest considerable net revenue from saffron and electricity production in five years, although challenges related to installation and upkeep remain for successful implementation.
title: Colorado researchers grow saffron on solar panels, double yield and make $60,000

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: The Federal Trade Commission has broadened eligibility criteria for Amazon Prime customer refunds related to misleading practices. Customers enrolled or attempted to cancel between specific dates may receive refunds automatically. Amazon will issue refunds up to $200, significantly increasing previously capped amounts. Eligible Prime customers do not need to take any action to receive their payments. Refunds will be sent by April 2027 through checks or electronic payments.
title: More Amazon Prime customers to get up to $200 from October 1

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Oregon has approved a $2 million purchase of Abiqua Falls, a famous 92-foot waterfall that was put up for sale by its private owner in February. The deal includes 160 acres of land and will bring the waterfall under state ownership, while officials work on plans for management, maintenance and public access.
title: Oregon approves $2m deal to protect 92-foot Abiqua Falls and open public access

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission has recalled approximately 51,000 lithium-ion battery packs from Blue Cactus Company. These battery packs, sold on Amazon, pose risks of overheating and potentially catching fire. Consumers who purchased the recalled packs should immediately stop using them and contact the company for replacements. Proper disposal methods are required due to the fire hazard associated with these batteries.
title: 51,000 chair battery packs recalled after overheating, smoking and fire reports

author: SANJAY SHARMA
description: Dr Monish Kanna R secured AIR 1 in NEET PG 2026 with 641 out of 720 marks after a preparation journey built around consistent practice and repeated revision. He attempted 10,425 MCQs across 445 leaderboards, finishing Rank 1 in 85, and revised his workbooks four to five times. Despite facing burnout after a disappointing result, he recovered through better study habits, rest and family support. His strategy focused on analysing mistakes, revising consistently and maintaining discipline.
title: Who is Dr Monish? NEET PG 2026 AIR 1 scores 641 out of 720

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
title: US returns 36 ancient Syrian artifacts worth over $5 million

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: Mark Zuckerberg's impressive superyacht, Launchpad, has recently anchored in Japan, right beside Yusaku Maezawa's Nausicaä. Their close proximity underscores an ongoing legal dispute as Maezawa pursues Meta for the misuse of his name in deceptive investment advertising. Even without plans to meet, their vessels symbolize the intense rivalry. After a summer in Alaska, Launchpad is set to chart its course towards Singapore, making this encounter noteworthy.
title: Zuckerberg’s $300m superyacht docks in Japan, gets neighbour who once wanted Meta out

author: A SELVARAJ
description: Chennai police have established a Special Investigation Team to probe allegations of sexual offences against R Veeramani. The SIT will be led by Additional Commissioner of Police PC Thenmozhi and includes several key officers. Allegations expanded following the arrest of Veeramani and his associates, highlighting a severe situation. Investigators are analyzing evidence, including digital material linked to the case. The investigation continues as authorities seek further clarity on the events.
title: Veeramani POCSO case: All-woman SIT formed to investigate against granite baron

author: HIJAM RAJU SINGH
description: A significant upset struck India's badminton campaign as men's doubles duo Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, seeded fourth, fell to an unexpected defeat in the opening round. They began impressively with a 21-12 victory in the first game but struggled to maintain this lead, losing the second game 21-19 to their Thai opponents.
title: Asian Games: Defending champions Satwik-Chirag suffer shock first-round exit

author: VIVEK DUBEY
title: SIR row: Plea in SC seeks prosecution of CEC Gyanesh Kumar, SIT inquiry

author: AADRITA HALDER
title: SIR row: Cong workers protest against CEC; cops use water cannons in Patna, Chandigarh

author: SHREEDHAR RATHI
description: A 17-year-old girl experienced a disturbing incident on her birthday inside Aastha Kunj Park. After visiting Kalkaji Mandir, she and her friend were approached by three men claiming to be police officers. The men allegedly assaulted the girl at knife point in various locations within the park. After the attacks, they threatened her and her friend to remain silent about the incident.
title: ‘Gun nikal’: Delhi victim recounts how rapists took turns, held knife to her neck

author: VIVEK DUBEY
title: Tarun Tejpal challenges rape conviction, SC seeks Goa govt response

author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
description: During a recent press conference, Baba Ramdev addressed questions about the authenticity of Patanjali's cow ghee. He emphasized that by utilizing various milk by-products, the company can offer competitive prices. According to Ramdev, India's significant contribution to global milk production ensures that no milk goes to waste post butter extraction, resulting in the creation of various dairy products that enhance their value and support Patanjali's pricing model for cow ghee.
title: Baba Ramdev explains why cheaper ghee does not always mean fake ghee

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: At just nine years old, Adrian Abraham is on a mission to pass a Grade 8 electric guitar exam in the UK, setting his sights on becoming the youngest achiever of this goal for a Guinness World Record. With a fervor for rock and metal music, he not only showcases his talents on stage but also creatively blends Indian music with Western rock on social media.
title: Meet Adrian Abraham, 9, aiming for world record with Grade 8 guitar exam

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: At just 12 years old, Minnesota's Natalie Flaherty launched the 'I Stand With Anne' campaign, aimed at fighting hate in all its forms. She crafted more than 100,000 bracelets featuring her powerful message, spreading awareness across the globe. Through successful partnerships with organizations dedicated to Holocaust remembrance, Flaherty earned the prestigious 2026 Gloria Barron Prize. This passionate advocate plans to distribute more bracelets this Halloween, continuing her mission.
title: Minnesota girl, 12, sent 100,000 bracelets to 50 countries, won $10,000 prize

author: ARYAN SINGH
description: In a surprising move, US President Donald Trump has directed the Navy to switch back to steam catapults for new aircraft carriers. This retracement comes even as contracts are being awarded to enhance the Electromagnetic Aircraft Launch System. With substantial work already in progress on USS Doris Miller, reintroducing steam catapults may complicate design and operational aspects of modern carriers, particularly as China embraces electromagnetic technology on its new fleet.
title: Trump orders steam catapults, but US Navy keeps EMALS alive

author: DHRUV YADAV
description: The Indian Air Force is preparing to induct a new satellite-guided variant of the Smart Anti-Airfield Weapon. This upcoming weapon is designed specifically to target hardened ground installations like bunkers and runways. A contract worth Rs 810.79 crore has been signed for 160 units of the advanced weapon system. The development emphasizes indigenous capabilities, showcasing the government's commitment to enhancing local defense manufacturing.
title: Indigenous satellite guided weapon to give air force long range strike capability

author: NITESH DUBEY
description: Suruchi Singh and Kamaljeet made history for India by clinching its first-ever gold medal in shooting at the Asian Games. Their stellar teamwork in the mixed team event earned them a remarkable score of 484.6. Overcoming obstacles in the individual events, they also excelled during the qualification round. Suruchi's unwavering commitment and extensive training were pivotal to their triumph, marking a landmark achievement in Indian shooting.
title: Who is Suruchi Singh? 19-year-old who has won 5 WC golds and now an Asian Games title

author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
description: In a significant life choice, Preeti Bisnik has opted to leave her role at Deloitte and return to India. This decision comes as she wishes to dedicate more time to her ageing parents and address her own health challenges. The urgency of her mother's health concerns fuels her commitment to being present for her family. While she focuses on supporting her loved ones, Preeti is not rushing into new employment.
title: Woman quits high-paying Canada job after 6 years, returns to India for parents

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: In a touching tale of serendipity, a silver US Army ring lost for twenty years has been reunited with its owner, Terry Sheppard Jr. Found by Mary Thelen in her son's footlocker, she took it upon herself to track him down. Douglas, who served in Iraq, probably misplaced it while stationed at Fort Bragg, North Carolina.
title: US Army ring missing since 2006 returned to owner 20 years later

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: In a recent legal battle, A.B. Quintanilla III is taking his sister Suzette to court regarding the earnings from Selena's estate. Claiming entitlement to 25% of certain profits under a 1995 agreement, he alleges he hasn't received the complete payments for the past few years, while Suzette and their mother refute any accusations of misconduct, shedding light on the intricate handling of Selena's legacy.
title: Selena’s brother sues sister for over $1 million in legacy profits dispute

author: ROHITASHWA RANJAN
description: Zohran Mamdani, New York's first Muslim mayor, denounced Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's UN speech, alleging it promotes genocide against Palestinians. He pointed out that Netanyahu is facing an arrest warrant from the International Criminal Court for potential war crimes. Mamdani's strong stance reflects growing calls for accountability amidst protests around the UN, where nearly 100 people were arrested, highlighting the escalated tensions in the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.
title: 'Netanyahu used his speech to repeat baseless lies': Mamdani slams Israel PM's UN address

author: TOI BUSINESS DESK
description: More than 150 offers across 23 IITs are involved in the cases, with some companies withdrawing between 10 and 15 offers, AIPC convenor and IIT-Guwahati associate professor John Jose said.
title: IITs to bar 22 firms from campus hiring for 2 years after 150+ offers unhonoured

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: Under CEO Ali Ghodsi, Databricks has soared to a staggering $190 billion valuation. Ghodsi emphasizes reducing meetings to effectively confront the significant challenges that arise within the company. He engages in discussions multiple times weekly to uncover and resolve pivotal issues. Prominent figures, such as Jamie Dimon from JPMorgan Chase, also voice concerns regarding the culture of excessive meetings, indicating a collective push towards enhancing efficiency in the corporate landscape.
title: Databricks CEO reveals his key to scaling: Don’t keep top talent in meetings

author: AMIT KUMAR
description: Suruchi Inder Singh and Kamaljeet were in control from the start of the mixed team final. The pair scored 103.0 in the first series of Stage 1, followed by 202.4 and 303.5. They continued their strong performance in Stage 2, scoring 364.7 in the first series and staying comfortably ahead of South Korea and Iran.
title: 'Final mein gai, to gold hi layegi': Suruchi's coach after Asian Games gold

author: ROHITASHWA RANJAN
description: Union minister Chirag Paswan urged the Election Commission to take a firm stand amids rising criticism from opposition members. He highlighted the crucial need for the commission to maintain public confidence in the integrity of elections. In light of reported disagreements, opposition leaders are calling for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
title: 'EC must maintain trust of people': Chirag Paswan on SIR row

author: VIVEK DUBEY
title: Nationwide protests from Oct 2 if CEC doesn't resign by Saturday: CJP's Dipke

author: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK
description: Samantha Ruth Prabhu and her husband Raj Nidimoru are thrilled to welcome their first child soon. Alongside this joyous news, a nostalgic Class 10 report card showcasing her academic excellence has emerged online. With her pregnancy announcement, Samantha humorously reflected on her former scholastic achievements. As she embarks on the journey of motherhood, she seems poised to take a step back from her film endeavors.
title: Samantha Ruth Prabhu's Class 10 marksheet resurfaces: actress scored 887/1000 marks

author: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK
description: The iconic film 'Baashha', starring Rajinikanth, was born from a casual chat on the set of 'Hum' involving Amitabh Bachchan and Govinda. They brainstormed a police scene that never made it to the final cut. Inspired, Rajinikanth relayed this to director Suresh Krissna during 'Annamalai'. With their title in hand, they crafted 'Baashha', completing it in a mere five to six months.
title: Rajinikanth’s ‘Baashha’ idea was born from a scene discussed during ‘Hum’ shoot

author: SAURABH THAKUR
description: A consumer complaint was upheld by the Hyderabad district commission regarding a cancelled film show. The complainant experienced distress due to the abrupt cancellation of the movie after 10 minutes. The theatre management initially attributed the cancellation to low occupancy, and later to a technical issue. The commission found insufficient evidence supporting the theatre's claims for the show cancellation.
title: PVR Inox ordered to pay Rs 6,000 after movie show cancelled 10 minutes after start

author: YASHASVI VASISTHA
description: Delhi Development Authority has directed owners of older high-rise buildings to complete structural safety audits within three months. This directive applies to buildings sanctioned before March 21, 2001, with high footfall also included. Recent building collapses in Delhi have raised concerns about structural integrity and safety. The audit aims to assess the earthquake resistance of these buildings. Failure to comply may result in action against the owners.
title: Delhi’s old high-rises face mandatory structural safety audits under new DDA order

author: ARYAN SINGH
description: In a rallying call, Saudi Arabia's Grand Mufti has urged border troops to gear up for crucial sacrifices in the fight against the Houthi movement. He highlighted the necessity of reinstating Yemen's Saudi-backed administration amid escalating hostilities. Recent weeks have seen intensified assaults from both sides, with missile strikes increasingly threatening Saudi territory, as the Houthis target vital infrastructure and cities.
title: ‘Lives may be sacrificed’: Saudi Grand Mufti urges troops to fight against Houthis

author: PRIYANKA JAISWAL
title: 'Want China out of Tibet': Protesters rally in Washington amid Trump-Xi meet

author: VIVEK DUBEY
title: Iran offers US 7-day plan to end war, reopen Strait of Hormuz

author: HADI KHAN
description: The Mumbai Crime Branch has recorded statements from 20 individuals related to Sahil Wakode's death. Investigators have struggled to access details from Wakode's mobile phone, which is locked. The National Commission for Scheduled Castes is probing allegations of discrimination and harassment preceding his death. Wakode's family has demanded action against Professor Doolla while protesting at Azad Maidan. IIT Bombay has issued an apology regarding its earlier communications about the incident.
title: IIT-Bombay student's iPhone remains locked, professor's statement not recorded

author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
description: Harshit Mahawar claims that using incognito mode for office work has produced unexpected professional benefits. He believes it prevents employers from monitoring his browsing activity while working. Mahawar states he received better salary hikes and promotions as a result of this habit. He became the youngest employee to rise from a fresher to vice president in three years. However, there is no evidence that incognito mode directly influences career advancement.
title: Man says working in ‘incognito mode’ helped him get promoted; shares tips

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
description: Massachusetts is restoring Century Bog, a former cranberry farm in Plymouth and Wareham, to complete protection of Red Brook from White Island Pond to Buttermilk Bay. The restored wetland and stream channel could benefit about 60 conservation-priority species, including “salter” brook trout that move between freshwater and saltwater estuaries.
title: Massachusetts turns retired cranberry bog into habitat for rare brook trout

author: TOI REAL ESTATE DESK
title: Greg Norman bought Florida estate for $4.9m, sold it 30 years later for $55.1m

author: AADRITA HALDER
title: ‘Long skirts, good mothers': Italian minister sparks outrage over sexist remarks

author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
description: Introducing Vrishvardhan Sharma, a gifted nine-year-old from Bengaluru whose early mastery of the Bhagavad Gita has brought him into the national spotlight. He completed many Gita parayanas and memorized Panini’s Ashtadhyayi, showcasing his dedication. Beyond academic pursuits, he ventured into programming, creating impactful apps such as GitaVardhan and KannadaVardhan to connect people with ancient wisdom. His unique ability to merge age-old scholarship with contemporary innovation has garnered him various honors.
title: Meet Vishvavardhan Sharma, 9, who built an offline Gita app

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: Microsoft is shifting its communications strategy to enhance the roles of its employees in public messaging. The company will move its communications team under Brad Smith's organization, focusing on legal and public affairs. Satya Nadella emphasized the importance of employees who are closer to products in telling Microsoft's story. Frank Shaw, the longtime communications chief, will transition to an advisory role as part of this restructuring.
title: Microsoft shakes up communications team; CEO Satya Nadella sends memo to employees

author: SHIVANGHI PAYAL
description: During discussions with US leaders, Chinese President Xi Jinping emphasized the concept of the Thucydides Trap, advocating for peaceful coexistence between the two nations. His repeated calls for mutual respect convey Beijing’s desire to evade conflict with the US. Historical instances suggest that shifts in power do not inevitably lead to war. However, analysts remain split over the implications of the Thucydides Trap in the current US-China dynamic.
title: Athens to Washington: What is the ‘Thucydides Trap’ Chinese President Xi keeps invoking

author: PRIYANKA JAISWAL
title: Watch: Pakistan PM runs away from questions on Hafeez Saeed at UN

author: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK
description: Earlier this year, the Kansas City Current launched a free youth soccer league in the Northeast neighbourhood, aiming to give 120 children aged 8 to 10 access to the sport. Co-owner Brittany Mahomes supported the initiative. She also received United WE’s inaugural Champion for Change Award, recognising her leadership in women’s sports and community development, alongside the Mahomes family's philanthropic efforts through the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation.
title: Brittany Mahomes’ major recognition: How is she shaping KC Current’s rise?

author: TRENDING DESK
description: The United States has introduced stricter visa regulations aimed at curbing commercial birth tourism. Targeting those involved in these networks, the State Department highlights that seeking US citizenship through childbirth is not a legitimate basis for visitor visas. However, pregnant travelers visiting for valid purposes, like medical care, are not outright prohibited. Transparency during the visa process is crucial for all applicants.
title: US tightens visa rules on ‘birth tourism’: What Indian travellers need to know

author: PRIYANKA JAISWAL
title: Watch: Rainfall triggers major landslide in Sikkim's Rimbi

author: ARYAN SINGH
description: Iran has granted the United States a six-day window to address its conditions for re-establishing access to the Strait of Hormuz. Key points include the lifting of U.S. sanctions on Iranian ports and the release of frozen Iranian funds. British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has engaged with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi amid rising tensions.
title: Iran gives US six days to meet conditions for reopening Strait of Hormuz: Report

author: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK
description: Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce’s successful venture, Garage Beer, has received a new investment amid the star player's record breaking performance.
title: Kelce Beer Brand Valued: Garage Beer tops $200m after rapid growth; investors back expansion

author: VIVEK DUBEY
description: Donald Trump and Xi Jinping met at the White House to discuss key issues like trade and artificial intelligence. They agreed to extend their trade truce by two months while significant disputes remain unresolved. Taiwan and its security implications were also central to the discussions, as Xi urged caution regarding the island. Both leaders emphasized the importance of avoiding confrontation and fostering cooperation between their countries.
title: 'Let's race, not wrestle': 5 takeaways as Trump-Xi navigate trade, Taiwan and AI

author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
description: In a powerful recount, Ritica detailed her decision to resign after encountering workplace harassment, met with inadequate responses from management. Despite reporting the incidents to HR, her cries for help were dismissed, leading to even more obstacles, including pressure toward her coworkers to file complaints against her. Ultimately, she felt compelled to leave, convinced that the situation would remain unchanged.
title: "I complained and had to resign": Employee on cost of reporting harassment

author: VIVEK DUBEY
title: ‘Extreme tail risk’: Mark Carney says Canada considered risk of military attack by US

author: SHIVANGHI PAYAL
description: Dalal Street began trading on a positive note after experiencing a significant decline earlier this week. BSE Sensex opened over 100 points higher, while NSE Nifty traded above 23,000. However, rising crude oil prices are impacting overall market sentiment and limiting gains. Foreign investors have also contributed to the decline by selling Indian shares worth over 50 billion rupees.
title: Stock market today: BSE Sensex opens over 100 points up, NSE Nifty50 trades above 23,000

author: AMIT KUMAR
description: Russian pistol coach Yury Lisichko arrived in India in 2009 for a one-year assignment with the Indian Army. Years later, his Greater Noida workshop has become a stop for shooters seeking the right pistol grip. From Anish Bhanwala and Manu Bhaker to Jitu Rai and Sarabjot Singh, shooters have worked with Lisichko, who studies their hands, modifies fresh pieces of wood and keeps adjusting until the pistol and shooter work together.
title: From Russia to India: Meet Yury Lisichko, the man fixing shooters' pistol grips

author: ROHITASHWA RANJAN
description: In response to Pakistan's statements at the UN Human Rights Council about Kashmir, Indian diplomat Kshitij Tyagi asserted that Jammu and Kashmir is an integral part of India. He denounced Pakistan's occupation of the territory while drawing attention to the systematic violence faced by religious minorities in Pakistan. Furthermore, Randhir Jaiswal dismissed Pakistan's assertions about the Indus Waters Treaty, reinforcing India's steadfast stance amid ongoing bilateral tensions.
title: ‘Kashmiri Pandits driven out by Pakistan-backed terrorists’: India at UN

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: Intel has cut its vice president ranks from about 450 to 200 and halved management layers from 12 to six under CEO Lip-Bu Tan. CFO David Zinsner blamed a cultural problem of veto power and poor transparency for years of slow execution and delayed products. He said Intel 18A yields are ahead of schedule, 14A risk production is set for 2027, and gross margins have climbed into the low 40s.
title: Intel cuts VP ranks from 450 to 200; CFO says ‘cultural problem’ delayed products

author: TNN
description: A video reportedly showing a minor girl being harassed in Banka has emerged online. Following this incident, police registered a case against six unidentified youths for their actions. The video appears to have been recorded six months ago at Mandar Parvat tourist site, according to initial investigations. Similar incidents in Samastipur and Muzaffarpur have previously led to multiple arrests.
title: Bihar: After Jamui, Samastipur, another girl harassed in public at tourist site

author: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK
description: Vishal Chaturvedi's film 'Hanuman Ansh' has completed seven weeks in theaters, achieving significant box office success. On Day 49, the movie earned Rs 3.65 crore, enhancing its total India net collection to Rs 288.33 crore. The film's total worldwide gross collection stands impressively at Rs 377.05 crore, supported by overseas earnings. With varied daily collections throughout the week, it registered a high of Rs 13.75 crore on Sunday.
title: Hanuman Ansh Day 49 Tally: Film nets Rs 3.65 cr in India; worldwide gross hits Rs 377.05 cr

author: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK
description: Kunal Kemmu's 'VIBE' recorded Rs 90 lakhs in India on its seventh day at the box office. The Hindi action-comedy registered the collection across 1,984 shows on Thursday, September 24.
title: 'Vibe' Box Office Day 7: Film nets ₹11.35cr in week 1; worldwide gross hits ₹15.5cr

author: REEBA ZACHARIAH
title: Ex-CJI, more legal experts back Tata Sons on Chandra's reappointment

author: HADI KHAN
description: During a comedy event at Nirma University, a student's remark led to a confrontation with a professor. The professor allegedly grabbed the student's collar and issued a threat in response. The National Students' Union of India demanded an apology from the professor and called for an impartial inquiry into the incident. The university has not yet publicly responded to these demands or commented on the incident.
title: ‘Jaldi kar, Panvel nikalna hai’: Comedy show turns ugly at an Ahmedabad university

author: TIMESOFINDIA.COM
description: Terry Fox began his Marathon of Hope on April 12, 1980, running across Canada for cancer awareness. He trained for months, covering over 5,000 kilometres before starting his journey. Fox ran daily through various weather conditions, reaching communities to discuss cancer research. Unfortunately, on September 1, 1980, he had to stop running as his cancer spread to his lungs.
title: Meet Terry Fox: He lost his leg to cancer, then ran 5,373 km across Canada

author: PRIYANKA JAISWAL
title: UAE suspends Iranian airline flights, joins countries enforcing US sanctions

author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
description: As the son of celebrated actor R. Madhavan, Vedaant Madhavan gears up for the 2026 Asian Games, aiming to carve out his niche in the swimming world. Prioritizing the 200m freestyle over his usual long-distance events, Vedaant is committed to training hard. Despite facing the pressures of his lineage, he remains intensely focused, embodying the spirit of discipline and perseverance on this competitive journey.
title: Vedaant: Famous surname brings pressure, but I want my own identity in swimming

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Massachusetts car dealer Charles Fotopoulos bought a 1951 Nantucket cottage for $899,000 in 2021, knowing coastal erosion posed a serious risk. He said he would be satisfied if the property lasted five years. Five years later, the home remains standing, but only a few feet separate it from a 40-foot drop to the beach below, as erosion continues.
title: Man's $899K bet on Nantucket cliff cottage: Still standing 5 years later

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Chico has spent 38 years living alone deep in the Amazon, far from modern conveniences. He planted 1,500 Brazil nut trees, grows fruit, collects rainwater and hunts wild pigs for food. His extraordinary life was documented by the Yes Theory expedition team, who travelled deep into the rainforest to meet the man known locally for living in solitude.
title: Alone 38 years in Amazon, Chico plants 1,500 trees and builds his own world

author: SHIVANGHI PAYAL
description: Following a tumultuous week influenced by geopolitical unrest and supply worries, oil prices have dipped slightly. WTI crude now stands at $93.52 a barrel, while Brent crude has retreated to $105.80. Ongoing negotiations aim to address the Middle East conflict, which has considerably strained energy supplies. In Saudi Arabia, military operations have further heightened supply concerns, underscoring the persistent instability in the region impacting global oil markets.
title: Oil slips 1% as traders hope for US-Iran truce amid fresh attacks on Saudi pipeline

author: ARYAN SINGH
description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has reiterated the peaceful intent of the country's nuclear program, emphasizing that it is not designed for weapon development. He expressed Iran's willingness to cooperate with international inspections and reduce its stockpile of enriched uranium. Pezeshkian pointed to the US's preference for military action over diplomatic solutions as a key factor in escalating tensions, asserting that Iran's military stance is purely defensive.
title: ‘It is unholy, It is illegal’: Iran President Pezeshkian denies nuclear bomb ambition

author: NIRUPA VATYAM
description: At NALSAR University, a student-led group bravely hosted a solidarity screening of Umar Khalid's documentary, promoting vital discussions about justice and human rights. Previous showings at other universities were canceled amid intimidation and threats, raising concerns about censorship. Notably, the film lacks certification from the Central Board of Film Certification. The university's vice-chancellor stated that the screening was not officially sanctioned.
title: NALSAR students screen Umar Khalid documentary

author: NIKHIL SHARMA
description: Gautam was confronted by four men who allegedly attempted to rob him while he was driving. After managing to escape, he reported the incident at the New Colony police station with his associates. Upon being attacked at the police station, Gautam and his friends suffered various injuries during the confrontation. Police later apprehended the suspects, who had fled to a nearby hotel.
title: ‘They threatened to kill us’: Car attack, assault outside Gurugram police station

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Spanish Ranch, a historic 5,650-acre property from the 1843 Mexican land grant, is safely protected from any future development. This initiative not only bolsters sustainable agricultural practices but also safeguards diverse wildlife habitats. A dedicated fundraising campaign, achieving an impressive $1 million, was spearheaded by the California Rangeland Trust, supported by generous contributions from private donors and conservation programs.
title: Mexican land grant from 1843: 5,650-acre Cuyama ranch now protected

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Tech executive Shannon Burns can pursue £76 million in compensation from Gitpod after winning a disability discrimination case. Burns was dismissed after sleeping in a sauna during an Austria work trip after forgetting her room key. The tribunal rejected Gitpod’s bid to cap her claim at £1 million, while the company’s acquisition by OpenAI could affect her shares.
title: Tech exec who slept in sauna can pursue £76M from Gitpod, tribunal rules
